title: Mashashimuet
summary: Mashashimuet names the springs on the south side of Otter Pond in Sag Harbor. The place is associated with today's Mashashimuet Park and Otter Pond landscape, and the name was remembered through Montaukett and local Native knowledge shared with William Wallace Tooker.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Otter Pond coordinate from USGS/TopoZone-style listing; exact springs not mapped.
history_content: The history preserves Mashashimuet as a traditional name for Otter Pond and its springs. Stephen Pharaoh of Montauk and a Native woman remembered as Aunt Ollie were named as informants for the place-name tradition. Archaeological writing also connects the Otter Pond area with shell-heap and artifact evidence.
translation_content:
No separate linguistic translation is given in the available references. The name is described as belonging to Otter Pond and its springs rather than analyzed into a translated phrase.

Why Place Names Matter

“In every culture and language, people use place names to refer to locations and to communicate information about these places with others.”

— Yoko Kugo, Community Voices, Practices, and Memories in Environmental Communication (2022), Introduction, paragraph 1
whereintheworld_content: This blue marker uses an approximate modern point for Otter Pond in Sag Harbor. It marks the general pond-and-springs association and is not an exact spring or archaeological-site coordinate.
